title: Post-call: simultaneous session capacity & rate structure
text:
Post-call: simultaneous session capacity & rate structure

['From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@finledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: simultaneous session capacity & rate structure

Hi Elaine — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can turn this into a concrete pilot proposal for FinLedger.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workload: user-facing payment orchestration UI + backend reconciliation jobs.
- Traffic profile (high level): many short generation requests plus a large fraction of long-lived streaming sessions used for UI progress updates.
- Latency goals: P95 < 400ms for short requests; streaming startup ideally < 300–500ms.

Open questions we need to size capacity and rate limits:
1) Peak concurrent sessions (long-lived streaming) and 95th-percentile concurrent sessions during business hours.
2) Average tokens per request (short) and average streaming bytes per session.
3) Percent of calls that are streaming vs non-streaming.
4) Whether you plan connection reuse (HTTP/2 multiplexing) from your side or short-lived connections per request.
5) Any hard constraints (e.g., must run in a single region, compliance requirements).

Proposed next steps:
- If you can share the traffic numbers above (rough buckets are fine), we’ll send a 6-week pilot proposal with: baseline reserved capacity for concurrent sessions, a burst pool for seasonal spikes, and an initial ratecard showing tokens/sec and connection quotas.
- Marissa (solutions) and Ben (SE) will sketch a technical plan for connection pooling and prefix caching to reduce per-token cost.

I attached a draft worksheet (redwood-sim-session-qproposal.xlsx) with the fields we mentioned — feel free to fill the shaded cells and send back.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[rishi@redwood.com] | +1 (415) 555-0198

[Attachment: redwood-sim-session-qproposal.xlsx (xlsx)]', 'From: Elaine Park <elaine@finledger.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: FinLedger SRE <sre@finledger.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: simultaneous session capacity & rate structure

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the clear recap. Answers below (rough numbers from last quarter; will confirm with infra team tomorrow):

- Peak concurrent long-lived streaming sessions: ~350 (observed during product launch). Typical business-hour concurrent: ~80–120.
- Short requests: average tokens/request ~280, 95th percentile tokens ~1,200 when batch actions occur.
- Streaming ratio: ~60% of user-facing calls are streaming; backend reconciliation jobs are non-streaming.
- Connection model: current frontends use HTTP/2 with connection pooling to a sidecar; we can maintain long-lived connections and multiplex many logical sessions over a small number of TCP sockets.
- Constraints: single-region (us-west) for this pilot; SOC2 is in progress but not blocking the pilot.

We also need to understand how Redwood enforces connection-level quotas vs per-request QPS and token/sec ceilings. Can you outline how rate limiting would affect our burst scenarios (e.g., bulk imports + many users logging in)?

Attached: infra constraints doc and a short csv with sample hourly concurrent counts. We’d like a 6-week pilot with clear failure modes and a burst pool.

—Elaine
Head of Product, FinLedger
elaine@finledger.com

[Attachment: finledger-infra-constraints.pdf (pdf)]', "From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Elaine's numbers — need pilot design & ratecard

Forwarding Elaine's reply — she gave concrete concurrency numbers and confirmed HTTP/2 multiplexing on their side. Key asks: baseline reserved pool, 6-week pilot, burst pool, and clear failure modes.

Marissa / Ben — can you draft a short pilot plan that covers both the performance side and commercial (rate limits, burst pricing, pilot pricing)? Priorities:
- Technical: how we will support 350 peak concurrent streaming sessions while keeping startup latency target (P95 streaming startup < 500ms). Options: session pinning vs multiplexed channels, KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, and connection pooling guidance for their sidecar.
- Quotas: propose a baseline reserved concurrent sessions number, a soft burst pool with fallback to lower-cost model variants, and per-account tokens/sec ceilings.
- Commercial: 6-week pilot with crediting toward first 3 months of committed Dedicated capacity if they convert; show soft and hard rate limits and how alerts will be surfaced.

I attached a short note (redwood-conn-strategies.md) with initial SE recommendations. Feel free to edit and send directly to Elaine after we agree.

Thanks — R

[Attachment: redwood-conn-strategies.md (md)]", 'From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@finledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-19T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot proposal & next steps — FinLedger (FL-2028-042)

Hi Elaine — thanks for the quick turn. Based on your numbers, here’s a short pilot proposal we can start on next week:

Pilot scope (6 weeks)
- Reserved baseline: 250 concurrent streaming sessions (dedicated pool).
- Burst pool: additional 150 concurrent sessions available as soft-burst (auto-granted until global capacity signals); measured in 5-minute windows.
- Parallel short requests: support up to 6 parallel requests per connection; tokens/sec ceiling per account: 10k tokens/sec soft, 15k tokens/sec hard for pilot.
- Streaming: we’ll prioritize streaming startup on the reserved pool; fall back to a lower-cost variant for burst traffic with slightly higher latency (P95 + ~200–300ms).

Ratecard and commercials
- Pilot credit: first 6 weeks billed at pilot rate (50% discount); if FinLedger converts to a 12-month Dedicated commit within 30 days of pilot end, pilot fees credit toward the reserved capacity commit.
- Documented failure modes: connection exhaustion (will trigger 429 with Retry-After + supervised fallback), token ceilings (will return 429 until rate is reduced), and model-variant fallback when reserved pool exhausted.

Operational handoffs
- Marissa will run an onboarding call with your SREs to configure connection pooling and prefix caching hooks (we’ll provide the sidecar tuning doc).
- We’ll instrument alerts and a latency dashboard for the pilot.

If this looks good I can send the pilot order and the pilot SOW via DocuSign — here’s the short link to the pilot PO: https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&acct=12345&po=1

Next steps:
1) Reply with confirmation (approve pilot scope) or any edits to the baseline/burst sizing.
2) If approved, we’ll schedule the onboarding call (Marissa) and provision the reserved pool.

Thanks — excited to get this rolling.

Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
